english.title: Assault by beating of an emergency worker
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) assaulted **(..SPECIFY PERSON..), an emergency worker, namely **(..SPECIFY TYPE OF EMERGENCY WORKER..), acting in the exercise of

(A)_[his]_
(B)_[her]_

functions as such a worker, by beating

(C)_[him]_
(D)_[her]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 39 of the Criminal Justice Act 1988 and section 1 of the Assaults on Emergency Workers (Offences) Act 2018.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
unlawfully assaulted
an emergency worker
who was acting in the exercise of his / her functions as such a worker
by beating him / her

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) On the 28th June 2022, the penalty for offences under this section was increased on indictment from a maximum of 12 months imprisonment to 2 years imprisonment by section 2 of the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act 2022. For the offence applying before the 28th June 2022, see H19568.
(ii) This is an aggravated version of the offence in document H4302; committing assault against an emergency worker acting in the exercise of his / her functions as such as worker, carries a higher penalty, as per section 1 of the Assaults on emergency Workers (Offences) Act 2018.
(iii) This offence wording is for assault of an emergency worker by beating (battery); see offence wording document H19561 for common assault against an emergency worker by putting him / her in fear of immediate violence.
